facts.situation: James and Caroline Whitmore are joint clients. James sold his business in April; the transition has been busy and emotionally significant for both. The £850,000 completion payment has been received and is held in a solicitor's client account, but £200,000 is committed to repaying a bridging loan due shortly. A deferred earnout of up to £400,000 is payable over the next two years only if agreed revenue targets are met; none has been received and it is not guaranteed. Their objective is long-term growth and a tax-efficient base to replace James's income when he steps back from full-time work in about three years. Recommendations must be weighed against that goal. Agreed risk profile is 4, balanced to moderate. They have no current portfolio income requirement; possible consultancy work is unsettled. Future help with grandchildren's school fees and a possible charitable donation are aspirations only, with no action in this report. James is concerned about pension over-contributions.

actions.action: Repay James's bridging loan from the completion proceeds.
Top up James's Holloway ISA, H4-ISA-J, using his allowance for the new tax year.
Top up Caroline's Holloway ISA, H4-ISA-C, using her allowance for the new tax year.
Contribute to James's Brightwell SIPP, B4-SIPP-J, at an appropriate level within the applicable limits.
Contribute to Caroline's Brightwell SIPP, B4-SIPP-C, at an appropriate level within the applicable limits.
Add completion proceeds to the Holloway joint GIA, H4-GIA-HJ.
Disinvest a portion of the Holloway joint GIA, H4-GIA-HJ, and rebalance it; the sale is a disposal.
Place the remaining available completion proceeds into a new jointly held investment account.
Retain the Meridian offshore bond, M4-BOND-J, unchanged and revisit it at the next review.
